title: Training associative memories may increase integration of composite systems

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Training associative memories may increase integration of composite systems

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Levin proposes that memories belonging to a collective (e.g. a rat's lever–reward association, which no single cell experiences) may help reify the collective Self, and that training associative memories into gene regulatory networks should be tested for increases in integrated information (self-coherence).

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 7. A Continuum: From Thoughts to Thinkers

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This is currently being investigated in the context of our training of associative memories into gene-regulatory networks and other substrates, with measures of integrated information to determine if the forming of memories increases the self-coherence of composite systems.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “7. A Continuum: From Thoughts to Thinkers”. Scope: Gene regulatory network models and other composite systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-15: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.46

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prediction can be made explicit and tested computationally, but the needed matched training outputs and integration measurements are not known to be public. Existing network models alone do not resolve it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Train matched gene-regulatory-network models with and without an associative memory, then compare preregistered integrated-information or self-coherence measures while controlling network activity and complexity. A reproducible increase specific to learned association supports the prediction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The paper describes the test as ongoing.

Integrated-information measures are contested and computationally difficult.

No known public dataset contains the required before-and-after training comparison.

fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.2
discriminating power: 0.65
data existence: 0.2
operationalizability: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The gene-network half of the proposal is now a re-runnable analysis: public code applies associative training to deposited biological models and scores causal emergence against random controls. That does not cover the behavioral example or the claim about reifying a collective Self, and a different integration measure could disagree. The testable network prediction is in good shape; the full statement is only partly resolved by it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Train published gene-regulatory network models on an associative conditioning protocol without rewiring them, and compare an integration measure before and after training against untrained and random-network controls. A reliable increase supports the network prediction; no increase, or an equal increase in untrained controls, refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The code covers network models, not a rat's lever-reward memory or a collective Self.

Results depend on the training schedule and on how network state is coarse-grained.

Causal emergence is one operationalization of integrated information and need not match other phi-style measures.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.7
data adequacy: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.8
data existence: 0.85
discriminating power: 0.65
